production_signing.private_key_storage: Five concealed base64 PKCS#8 DER Ed25519 values in one 1Password Developer Environment; no private key, environment ID, item reference, or secret is stored in the repository.
production_signing.local_route: 1Password injects one selected private identity only into the local release-signing child process. The signer binds the expected public key, signs exact release bytes, self-verifies, and creates a new envelope without overwrite.
production_signing.revocation_policy: Omission from the compiled production registry means revoked and quarantines affected active artifacts. A rotated identity always receives a new publisher key ID.

completion.trust_and_startup: Only five immutable public identities and exact ceilings are compiled. Raw caller-supplied trust APIs are crate-private. Normal startup reconciles reviewed tasks and re-verifies active artifacts before services or the scheduler become available; missing trust is classified as revoked and fails closed.
completion.lifecycle_and_ui: Users can verify and stage one bounded regular .jspack file, review immutable publisher and release facts, activate or roll back against exact target permissions, disable, re-enable, remove, retry cleanup, and follow truthful recovery guidance. Unknown or contradictory renderer projections fail closed.
completion.reviewed_execution: Static Skills are reloaded and reverified before display. Evidence Reviewer and Packet Builder preparation and execution bind exact current pack generation, context, approval, input digest, fixed local plan, single-use task, and durable bounded receipt. No shell, arbitrary filesystem, network, credential, external send, answer fill, or submission path exists.
completion.g19_quality_bar: The user approved a composed v3.0 bar: official Agent Skills specification conformance, deterministic static-package readiness, complete safe resources, a validated advisory Evidence Reviewer handoff, and an independently evaluated deterministic Evidence Reviewer target. Both evaluators expose only fixed target names and aggregate counts.
completion.signing_route: The Node standard-library signer consumes an environment or standard-input private key, derives and checks the exact public identity, preserves signed release bytes, self-verifies the Ed25519 signature, never overwrites output, and has a Rust interoperability vector.

red_green.initial_red: Fail-first Rust, TypeScript, and script tests proved missing production trust, startup reconciliation, signer, official YAML validation, staging, lifecycle, reviewed execution, receipt, accessibility, and G19 handoff behavior before implementation.
red_green.review_red: Independent reviews found caller-injectable public trust APIs, incorrect target-release facts, stranded pending approvals, case identity races, replay copy drift, weak receipt decoding, missing keyboard and focus routes, silent availability states, static dev-profile drift, and a production compile lint. Each received the smallest focused regression and correction.
red_green.green: The corrected implementation passed focused regressions, the complete frontend and script suites, full Rust workspace gate, official upstream validator, production build, and all repository policy checks.

retained_gaps.gap: No Windows 11 machine was available. Native ACL ownership and privacy, reparse rejection, pack persistence and rollback, chooser behavior, and installed focus behavior remain unverified live. The user explicitly accepted this risk for Milestone 7.
The native chooser, drop, and approval-focus paths have contract and component evidence on macOS 27, but still require installed macOS 26 accessibility and release-matrix proof.
Generic scripts and dynamic pack adapters remain deferred. Transition-only v3 names and pre-v3 compatibility machinery remain owned by line closure.
